In the Draft Report, it is stated that the CRA will incorporate all necessary and appropriate noise controls in the development guidelines to which developers must conform under the previsions of the Urban Renewal Plan, as amended. However, without establishing appropriate critical noise standards, mere application of the noise controls may not provide an effective measure to minimize all the the potential adverse noise impact. The Final Report, therefore, should include established critical noise standards which will most effectively abate noise problems. These standards should not be limited to the various proposed land use development but should also be expanded to include construction activities. To minimize the added noise impacts of increased traffic, the final report should also discuss and established truck routes and time restructions, if appropriate.
II. AIR QUALITY
The air quality impact study in the Draft report briefly summarizes the conclusions of the Boston Transportation Control Program (TCP) and the state motor vehicle emissions inspection program (I&M) to the Kendall Square development. Since these as well as other such strategies, such as a "parking freeze" and "Masspool" would help enhance air quality and traffic congestion in the area, the CRA should establish an implementation program to comply with othese programs. The implementation procedure should be outlined in the Final EIR.
Regarding air quality emissions, the I&M program and the EPA's motor vehicle emission factors need further clarification. In first place, the Final EIR should more specifically spell out the proposed 10% emission reduction through implementation of the I&M program. Secondly, the EPA's revised emission factors - Supplement 5 - estimates now indicate (a) CO emissions higher than previously estimated and (b) CO emissions which deteriorate more rapidly in subsequent years. In light of this, the impact of these new emission factors should be investigated in the Final EIR.
III TRAFFIC IMPACTS
The review of the traffic study reveals that streets that may encounter increased congestion and air pollution are Broadway (+17%) and Third Street (+29%) outside the project area. Because Third Street traverses East Cambridge and the Middlesex Court House area, traffic congestion in this area is very likely. In the Final Report, therefore, the traffic study should be expanded to include peak hour traffic flows in the entire project impacted area, as well as several other key intersections which today suffer peak hour congestion and are important access routes to and from Kendall Square e.g.
(a) McGrath/O'Brien Highway and Commercial Avenue
(b) McGrath/O'Brien Highway and Third Street
(c) Longfellow Bridge heading towards Boston (PM Peak)
(d) Harvard Bridge, heading toward Boston (PM Peak)
(e) Vassar Street and Memorial Drive
(f) Lafayette Square/Central Square, Cambridge
